rule: DESC is the rule's words. The converter walks the record's token closure in PCGen application order (copy-base row, then the base row, then every `.MOD` row in file order -- NOT the order `data.raw_tokens` stores, which is base, copy-base, mods) and keeps a running list of DESC segments. For each DESC token: (1) split on `|`; (2) pop trailing segments while they match `!?PRE[A-Z0-9]+:` -- these are gates, not arguments; (3) count the highest `%N` the first segment references (a `%%N` counts as a candidate); (4) the last N pipe-segments are the arguments, taken from the RIGHT so a ` | ` table separator inside prose survives; when N is 0 one trailing TIGHT `|tag` (no whitespace either side) is stripped; (5) argument N is resolved: an integer literal -> Const; a bare name that is a same-row `DEFINE:X|<int>` -> Const (3,936 of 5,220 DESC bare-var args corpus-wide are this shape); `<Name>+/-<int>` with a same-row literal -> Const; anything else (1,284 external names, 1,538 formulas such as `max(MesmeristLVL/2,1)`) is handed to the formula lane and becomes a prose SLOT holding an Expr, never dropped; `%CHOICE`/`%LIST` become a Choice slot (see the `%CHOICE / %LIST` row); (6) `%%` collapses to `%` except `%%N` where argument N exists (then it is argument N -- 4 upstream rows, e.g. Water Jet); a bare `%` is kept only after a digit or as `d%` percentile dice, otherwise it is an unresolvable placeholder and is REFUSED (31 corpus rows); (7) `&nl;` `&lbracket;` `&rbracket;` `&pipe;` `,` decode to their characters (`:` appears in TEMPDESC and must be added); (8) a gate whose operands are all same-row literals is decided at convert time (segment kept or discarded); a gate on character facts (PREVAR* on external names, PREABILITY, PRECLASS, PRERULE ...) becomes that SEGMENT's Applies (gap); (9) surviving segments are joined with a single space in application order. A DESCISPI:YES record contributes NO DESC text (see NAMEISPI/DESCISPI row). The final prose string is blacklist-scanned with pi_screening::classify_field; a hit refuses the record, never ships the marker.
expr_shape: n/a for the words; each unresolved argument is a slot whose Expr the formula lane supplies (e.g. `10+INT` -> Sum([Const(10), AbilityMod(Int)]))
expr_gaps: prose slots: `prose: String` cannot carry a character-dependent term; need `prose: Vec<ProseSegment>` or `prose: String` + `slots: Vec<Expr>` with `{0}`-style anchors, so the live evaluator prints `DC 15` INSIDE the sentence (decisions.md §1 rule 1) instead of the converter dropping the term as render_pcgen_desc does today

per-segment Applies: one DESC/ASPECT/SPROP segment can carry its own PRE* gate (`Three|PREVARLTEQ:...` vs `%1|...|PREVARGTEQ:...`); SheetRule has ONE `applies` for the whole rule; need `ProseSegment { text, applies: Option<Applies> }` or the segment is refused

spell short/long text: `!PRERULE:1,DisplayFullSpell` segment is the one-line summary, the `PRERULE:1,DisplayFullSpell` segment the full text; SheetRule has no `summary` field -- add `summary: Option<String>` or drop the summary (open question)
applies_shape: none from the prose itself; per-segment PRE* gates on a DESC segment feed the segment's own Applies (prereq lane owns the PRE grammar)

rule: `.CLEAR` erases every DESC segment accumulated so far in APPLICATION order and nothing after it; `.CLEARALL` is the same for the whole token family. It is meaningful only with row boundaries, which `data.raw_tokens` throws away, so the converter MUST read the closure as rows (`wiring_class::token_closure_rows`) and apply copy-base -> base -> .MOD; on a `.COPY=` row the pattern is `DESC:.CLEAR\tDESC:<new text>` on the copying row itself (13 Horror Adventures/AP equipment rows). Two closure defects the converter must NOT inherit: (a) `build_mod_index` walks `_pfs/` (Pathfinder Society overlay) files whose `.MOD` rows are gated `!PRECHARACTERTYPE:1,PC` -- they never apply to a PC and must be excluded (215 corpus records carry PFS overlay tokens today); (b) the index keys `.MOD` rows by bare name with the `CATEGORY=` prefix stripped, so `CATEGORY=FEAT|Scribe Scroll.MOD` attaches to the CATEGORY=Special Ability record `Sorcerer Bloodline Feat ~ Scribe Scroll` whose display name is `Scribe Scroll` -- match on (category, name) and on KEY, never on display name alone.
applies_shape: none (the row's own PRE* on a `.MOD` row gates whether the whole row applies)
prose_effect: discards earlier prose; the converter never emits the literal `.CLEAR` (render_pcgen_desc has no guard for it and would print `.CLEAR` today)

Same tokenisation, argument, gate, escape and entity rules as DESC (111 BENEFIT tokens carry `%N`, 120 carry a `|` tail). Prose = DESC segments, then BENEFIT segments, application order, joined with one space; when DESC is PI-redacted (DESCISPI:YES) prose = BENEFIT alone -- the shipped `codex_named_unit_*` records already have exactly this shape. `BENEFIT:.CLEAR` (9 corpus records; 12 of the 14 tree rows are `_pfs/` overlay) follows the DESC:.CLEAR rule. rule: `ASPECT:<Name>|<text>[|<arg>...][|<PRE gate>...]`. The sub-key is a display label, mechanical per sub-key: for a display sub-key the text goes through the DESC substitution rules (2,040 of 2,387 bare-var ASPECT args are same-row DEFINE literals -> Const; 213 formulas -> slots; gates -> per-segment Applies) and is appended to prose as its own line `<Label>: <text>` after DESC/BENEFIT/SPROP, in application order. Multiple ASPECTs with the same sub-key and mutually exclusive PREVAR gates (Psychic Strike's `(1d6, DC %2)` vs `(1d6+%2, DC %3)`) are alternative segments: decided at convert time when the gate names a same-row literal, else per-segment Applies. A redacted sub-key (`ASPECT:[redacted PI]`, 118 corpus-wide) contributes nothing and is recorded in provenance. Today's ingester lifts ASPECT into `data.description` for NO kind; the converter reads the token, not the field.

In prose they are Choice slots: made -> the chosen record's label (a spell/skill/language/weapon NAME, not a number); unmade -> the words of the choice kind from a per-CHOOSE-type table (CHOOSE:SPELLS -> `a chosen spell`, CHOOSE:LANG -> `a chosen language`, CHOOSE:SKILL -> `a chosen skill`, CHOOSE:WEAPONPROFICIENCY -> `a chosen weapon`, CHOOSE:NUMCHOICES/others -> `a chosen option`); `%LIST` unmade -> plural form. render_pcgen_desc drops both today (`SD31-W6-INTEGRATE-001`); the converter must not. The choice lane owns the ChoiceId and the CHOOSE-type table; this lane owns only how the slot prints.
expr_gaps: Choice(ChoiceId) resolves to an integer in the schema; `%CHOICE`/`%LIST` print a NAME (the chosen spell/skill/language) -- need `Expr::ChoiceName(ChoiceId)` or a `ProseSegment::Choice(ChoiceId)` that renders the chosen record's label, and a per-CHOOSE-type table of the unmade words
prose_effect: the chosen name in the sentence, or the choice-kind words

instances: NAMEISPI 934, DESCISPI 529 of 21,722 non-DONE units joined to a corpus record (live docs/work-inventory.json 2026-09-07, 35 books excl. core_rulebook/ultimate_campaign, vehicle excluded; this lane's own join, same method as TOKEN-MODEL); corpus-wide NAMEISPI 1,177 (all `YES`), DESCISPI 686 (673 `YES`, 13 `Yes`) of 51,474 data/corpus records (39 book dirs, recursive walk, _parity excluded), 48,673 of them with a non-empty raw_tokens list; 2,330 records corpus-wide are stamped `license: PI-REDACTED`
rule: Product Identity flags never reach `prose` or `label`; they reach `provenance.pi`. Rule, mirroring pi_screening.rs: (1) `NAMEISPI:YES` -> label = codex neutral name (as shipped today, `codex_generated_name: true`), `provenance.pi.name_declared = true`; (2) `DESCISPI:YES` (case-insensitive value, per `declared_product_identity`) -> every DESC segment is omitted from prose, `provenance.pi.description_declared = true`; BENEFIT/ASPECT/SPROP/SAB are NOT covered by DESCISPI and stay; (3) the final `prose` and `label` strings are scanned with `classify_field`'s 60-term blacklist (union rule: declaration OR term hit); a hit on `label` refuses the record (a name cannot be redacted), a hit on `prose` refuses the record -- the converter never writes `[redacted PI]` into prose because a marker on the sheet is not what a player writes; (4) provenance derives from the TOKENS, not from the record's `pi_field` stamp -- 50 corpus records carry `[redacted PI]` in a token with `pi_field: null`, and 253 have a redacted description without DESCISPI (term hits). A record whose only prose is PI keeps `SheetValue::Text` with empty prose and the label; it is sheet-complete (there is nothing the player may write).
prose_effect: removes DESC from prose; forces the neutral label; refuses on a blacklist hit

rule: VISIBLE decides whether the held rule is PRINTED. PCGen semantics: YES (default) = UI and export; NO = neither (internal bookkeeping rows: trackers, `CATEGORY:Internal`, equipmod codes); DISPLAY = UI only, not export; EXPORT = export only; QUALIFY = shown only once prerequisites are met (i.e. hidden in the picker until qualified, printed when held). Sheet rule: `print = VISIBLE != NO`. DISPLAY rows (2,319) are printed too: a player writes `Scribe Scroll (bonus feat)` on paper even though PCGen suppresses the class-feature row because the feat itself prints. The rule is still converted and held (it may grant or gate) -- it just carries `print: false` (gap). `DISPLAY|READONLY` = DISPLAY.
expr_gaps: no `visible`/`print` flag on SheetRule: VISIBLE:NO rules must be held (they grant/gate) but not printed
applies_shape: none (QUALIFY is a picker-side hint; the prereqs themselves are the prereq lane's Applies)
